hook: He Burned His Enemy's Letters Without Reading Them
text: In the year one hundred and seventy-five, a general named Avidius Cassius heard a false rumour that Marcus Aurelius was dead, and declared himself emperor. Three months later the rebellion collapsed. The historian Cassius Dio tells us what Marcus did next. When the letters of the rebel were brought to him, letters that might have named every secret supporter, he had them burned without reading them. He did not want to know. He did not want to spend the rest of his life suspecting his friends. He wrote to himself that the best way to avenge yourself is not to become like the one who wronged you.
